significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that a query-independent temporal anchor and a query-specified time signal are distinct internal variables whose magnitude imbalance predicts whether stored time-correct knowledge is overridden, and that "suppressing the default-anchor direction" selectively restores that knowledge. This combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling—failures vary with year distance, answer frequency, and the anchor/query signal ratio—with a form-(ii) causal mechanism, constraining explanations of temporal errors and predicting which stored facts will fail rather than merely showing that time is decodable. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and its mechanism; a negative result would rule out the proposed two-signal competition account in favor of ignorance, a unitary temporal axis, or other retrieval mechanisms, although failure to verify storage alone would be less discriminating. Gurnee and Tegmark's "Language Models Represent Space and Time" and Dhingra et al.'s work on time-aware language models show that temporal representation and changing factual knowledge are operational concerns; after topic substitution, those broad concerns alone would not merit this score, while the claim-specific predictive law and causal competition do.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two explicit handles: "the imbalance between anchor and query-time signal magnitudes predicts override on held-out facts" as a diagnostic predictor, and "suppressing the default-anchor direction" as an inference-time intervention. The predictor is ex ante when read before answer emission and can flag or gate a likely temporal-recall failure, while suppression provides an action window for systems that audit or serve time-scoped answers rather than only a post-hoc explanation. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion still predicts the direction of the distance/frequency and signal-imbalance relationships, and the hypothesis is asserted across multiple relations and model families, though its practical scope remains narrow to mutable temporal facts and does not promise a general knowledge-editing method. Under topic substitution, generic knowledge-retrieval research would not provide either handle or this transferable relation, so the reach score comes from the claim rather than the topic.
